extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), unit commanders, installation public affairs staffs, and other Army personnel responsible for public affairs and community outreach
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Army public affairs activities, releases, use of military assets, community outreach, and constraints on publicity and participation in public events. Covers what may be released, approval authorities, procedures, and content/behavior constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarded information — nonreleasable
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguarded information contained in paragraphs 7–19b(1) through 7–19b(3) is generally not releasable in any phase of unit activations, inactivations, redesignations, reorganizations, training, or movements within CONUS or OCONUS except as provided in paragraph 7–19c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of safeguarded information include: (a) Exact personnel strength and composition of units; (b) Status, amounts, or quality of equipment; (c) Combat efficiency; (d) Deployment of units to combat areas. Release requires compliance with paragraph 7–19c or other specified exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release protocol for Reserve Component unit actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When an activation, inactivation, redesignation, or reorganization involves a Reserve Component (RC) unit, information will be released according to specified authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. Army Reserve units: ARHQ–FB will release information about the local unit. Army National Guard units: CNGB will ensure NGB notifies the unit and the state adjutant general may release local-unit information once notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: HQDA coordination for activations involving other nations
rubrics_metrics.description: When an activation or restationing involves another nation, HQDA-level coordination is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with the ASCC, COCOM, U.S. Embassy PA teams, and the appropriate host nation authority prior to release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation activation/inactivation/realignment announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate and timely information, consistent with security and AR 5–10 policies, will be released to the public when the decision has been made to activate, inactivate, or realign an installation, facility, or activity and associated personnel reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for initial announcements are made at HQDA through OSD when the action requires prior notification of Congress because it: (a) will go into effect near-term or by attrition over an 18- to 36-month period; (b) involves reductions due to commercial activity actions; (c) involves accessing Government installations or facilities; (d) has generated congressional or public interest; or (e) was subject to public controversy during decision-making. OCPA may make exceptions to announcement levels, will issue guidance prior to scheduled announcement dates, commanders must avoid statements that invite speculation about inactivations/realignments/strength reductions, and commanders must provide a mechanism for public feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and movement release authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on unit training or movement that is not safeguarded may be released by the responsible commander, with special rules for major/joint exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial release of information on major Army exercises will be made at HQDA through OSD; initial release on major joint exercises will be made by OSD with later announcements by the joint commander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographing military installations or equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Public access and photographing of Army installations and items are subject to local command determination and security law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographing historical buildings or areas of public interest for private use is generally permitted but may require local command approval. Ground or aerial photographs, sketches, or graphic representations of classified military equipment or installations designated as restricted areas are punishable by law (18 USC 795) unless reviewed and cleared for release by proper authorities; reproducing, publishing, or selling such material without clearance is also punishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate media requests for foreign military students
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview requests about foreign military personnel attending U.S. Army schools must be coordinated for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate interview requests with the proper country’s senior officer in residence for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on premature release of Army studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Premature release of emerging results of Army studies and analyses before official approval is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only after official approval may results or analyses be publicly released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of information by contractors and commercial entities — permitted vs. excepted information
rubrics_metrics.description: Army policy is to make available maximum accurate information on Army contractual relationships and accomplishments, subject to explicit exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include: (1) Safeguarded information and data that offers unfair competitive advantage; (2) Nonexportable commercial information or data subject to arms-control export restrictions; (3) Information about materiel on the Militarily Critical Technologies List (MCTL). PAOs must not release material implying DA endorsement of a commercial firm/product/service, comparisons of materiel merits, DoD specification details or acceptance test results, or information involving critical military technology. Public release clearance at the lowest responsible level is authorized and encouraged; when higher-headquarters release is required or in doubt, PAOs should forward proposed material and recommendation to OCPA for HQDA/OSD coordination. Procedures for review/clearing are in appendix E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community outreach as a PA command function
rubrics_metrics.description: Community outreach supports relationships between military and civilian communities and is a command public affairs function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View communication as a social process of dialogue and interaction; PA teams should proactively facilitate communication with American and international publics, including key leaders, in all operations environments at home and abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and policy basis for PA planning and event participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for planning/conducting Army PA activities and evaluating requests are based on public law, Executive Orders, DoD directives, and DA regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army PA in coordination with SJA will leverage means to foster relations with veteran and military service organizations and nonprofits under guidance in 10 USC 2670 and 10 USC 2667 and current DoD directives. Questions on fundraising/membership drives or other legal matters should be referred to local SJA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and non-discrimination requirements for official participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Army participation in public events is conditioned on strict adherence to ethics rules and equal opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to 5 CFR 2635, DoD 5500.07-R and sound judgment. Official participation may be authorized only if admission, seating, and other accommodations are available to all Servicemembers and provide an environment free from harassment and unlawful discrimination. Installation activities and, when possible, off-installation activities must be open to all military personnel and their Families to the fullest extent permitted by law and DoD policy. See AR 600–20 for extremist organization guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for support to public events
rubrics_metrics.description: Support to public events must primarily or mutually benefit the Department of the Army and satisfy specific conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (1) Support cannot interfere with official duties or detract from readiness/training; (2) No additional fee may be charged specifically to observe Army participation (a general admission fee does not necessarily preclude participation if Army support is incidental and criteria are met); (3) Other statutes/regulations must not restrict Army participation; refer legal questions to local SJA and consider DoD 5500.07-R and AR 600–29 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD-coordinated multi-service events
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one service is involved in a public event, DoD may appoint a coordinator to manage multi-service participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATSD (PA) may appoint a DoD representative; when a DoD coordinator is appointed, Army participation is coordinated in advance through OCPA. This policy does not apply to MDW when it acts as DoD coordinator for National Capital Region events. OCONUS coordinated activities must be processed through the respective COCOM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of military assets for public affairs — authorization and request procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders are encouraged to provide military marching units, bands, color guards, ceremonial units, aerial demonstrations, static displays, and similar assets for public events; requests requiring higher approval must be forwarded through command channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that require DoD or DA approval go to OCPA. For ARNG units, send requests to NGB–PA. Local event sponsors submit requests using DD Form 2535 (Request for Military Aerial Support) or DD Form 2536 (Request for Armed Forces Participation in Public Events (Non-Aviation)) to the nearest military installation and forward through command channels as required. ASCC commanders with troops assigned TDY or deployed OCONUS may authorize non-aerial participation using resources under theater command control or with concurrence of the parent command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Army musical, ceremonial, and troop asset support participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Army musical, ceremonial, and troop units may support certain types of official and civilian events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized participation includes: (a) Official military functions; (b) Official civil ceremonies/functions sponsored by government entities (including overseas equivalents); (c) Civilian-sponsored public events to stimulate interest in the Armed Forces, support recruiting, patriotism, or national holidays; (d) Civilian-sponsored social/civic/cultural events where musical participation is patriotic and clearly an Army appearance; (e) Traditional military events fostering morale and welfare (e.g., military balls, dining-ins) per 10 USC 974; (f) Sports events under specified conditions (regular season military team competition, amateur local/regional events with incidental Army support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for shopping center/mall recruiting support
rubrics_metrics.description: Local commanders may authorize band/musician participation in shopping centers/malls to support recruiting under specific guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (1) All musicians must be in uniform clearly identifying them as Army musicians; (2) Community engagement must not be advertised or presented as promotion for the shopping center or special business activities (e.g., sales); (3) Primary purpose must be to gain attention and attract visitors to recruiting displays; (4) The relationship between location/event and band members must not impact the Army unfavorably or contradict this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration limits for Army band participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Army band and musician participation duration is normally limited to protect personnel resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration will normally not exceed three days per event to ensure proper use of Army personnel and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited participation and remuneration restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on where and how Army musicians and units may participate and receive compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibitions include: (a) Army musicians on official duty prohibited from providing background/dinner/dance music at events funded solely by nonappropriated funds (exception: military welfare society under 10 USC 2566); (b) Bands/musicians on official duty prohibited from receiving remuneration for furnishing music away from an installation in competition with civilian musicians; (c) Unless authorized by law or DoD policy, Army bands/members may not receive pay for an official performance in support of public events; (d) Off-duty personnel not generally barred from paid outside performances unless complaint verified that they compete with local civilians; verified competitors may be barred from that employment; (e) All band personnel subject to 10 USC 974, DoD 5500.07-R, this regulation, and local off-duty employment rules; (f) Army participation not authorized for motion-picture premieres/regular movie presentations, fashion shows, golf tournament pin holders, or events sponsored solely for commercial interests; parades solely to support commercial/promotional aspects; civilian-sponsored beauty contests, political rallies, or similar events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tour procedures for Army bands
rubrics_metrics.description: Tours and travel by Army bands are governed by assigned touring areas and approval requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tour areas are assigned by ATSD (PA) and coordinated biannually. A band performing outside its assigned area requires OCPA, ATSD (PA), and military department approval. A tour is defined as a series of public performances requiring more than two nights TDY from home station. CONUS bands performing outside their area must coordinate with OCPA; bands stationed outside the U.S. must coordinate through channels with OCPA before scheduling U.S. public performances. CONUS bands require COCOM/ATSD (PA)/OCPA approval before performing outside the U.S. Band tours OCONUS normally will not exceed 15 days; single-location tours not exceed seven days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical support content and event limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical support must reflect patriotic/military purpose and respect limits on program content and event types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed support includes parades, concerts, choral presentations, patriotic openers and other Army music presentations. No event will receive support of more than one band or choral group from any service without ATSD (PA) approval. Musical support at nonfederal events limited to patriotic/military selections demonstrating professionalism and focusing on the Army presentation. Dinner/background/dance music not authorized at civilian-sponsored events unless sponsor is a military welfare society. Background/dinner music programs are authorized for official U.S. Government events funded by appropriated funds regardless of location. Memorial service support only if deceased authorized state funeral/customary military honors or ATSD (PA) approved. Musical units may not perform backup support for other entertainers away from installations unless featured and provided waiver/ATSD approval. U.S.-based Army musical units may perform OCONUS only with prior approvals from OCPA/ATSD (PA)/appropriate OCONUS commander and host nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonial unit standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for ceremonial units (color guards, drill teams, specialized units) used in civilian ceremonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ceremonial units may be activated per approved TO&E or TDA or composed of volunteers authorized by local commander. Locally authorized volunteer units should be well-trained, have professional bearing, and operate at no additional cost to the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color guard composition and foreign flag policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition rules for Joint Armed Forces Color Guards and rules for carrying foreign flags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, employ Joint Guard: two Army flag bearers (national and Army), one Marine, Navy, Air Force, and Coast Guard flag bearer, and one Army and one Marine rifleman as escorts. If a Joint Guard cannot be formed, the senior member of the senior service carries national colors (Soldiers carry colors when present). Army personnel may carry flags of foreign nations in official civil ceremonies only when an official of that nation is present in an official capacity for whom honors would normally be rendered. In all other public programs, Army personnel in uniform and in an official capacity are not authorized to carry flags of foreign nations, veterans groups, or other nonmilitary organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and constraints for aerial demonstrations (flyovers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines flyovers and sets nonwaivable constraints for flyover support in PA missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoDI 5410.19, Vol.1 defines flyover as straight and level flight by no more than four military aircraft of same type over a predetermined point, not involving aerobatics. Constraints: (1) Event/observance must be of sufficient size/significance to justify use of Army aircraft and flown in conjunction with previously scheduled training at no additional expense; (2) Event should benefit the Army, have significant community interest, and be patriotic; (3) Aerial demonstrations must be planned with a PA communication plan to highlight Army capabilities; (4) Event sponsors must agree to formally recognize supporting units/crewmembers; (5) Flyovers only between local sunrise and sunset; (6) No flags, banners, streamers, or external loads may be attached/suspended from Army aircraft during flyover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerial demonstration request timelines and approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing, forms, and approvals required for flyover and other aerial demonstration requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All flyover requests must use DD Form 2535 and be received no later than 40 calendar days before the event. Aerial activities other than flyovers (tactical demonstrations) must be received 60 calendar days in advance and include a risk assessment and concept of operations approved at appropriate levels and acknowledged by the senior commander. Senior commanders must certify compliance with applicable policy/regulatory requirements before submitting; senior commanders may approve mission execution only after concurrence from OCPA. CNGB will ensure state adjutants general certify compliance in writing before submitting ARNG flyover requests. Vice Chief of Staff, Army may suspend a command's authority to approve flyover support for failures to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for qualifying air shows and outdoor events
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which aerial demonstrations (air shows, static displays, parachute teams) may be authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include: (1) Logistical support must not interfere with official duties or detract from readiness; (2) Army community engagement or legitimate PA/military training interests served; (3) Involvement is in the best interest of DoD; (4) Event is of interest/benefit to the local civilian community, ACOM, or other DoD organizations; (5) ACOM/organization able/willing to provide similar support to comparable events sponsored by similar nonfederal entities; (6) Participation not restricted by other statutes/regulations; (7) No admission fee (beyond reasonable sponsorship costs) for the event or the portion supported, or DoD/Army support is incidental to the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising event participation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions allowing aerial demonstrations at broadly based fundraising or charity events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be performed if events focus on the community as a whole; Army/DoD support should be incidental to the overall event or for-profit organizations must donate at least half of excess revenues to local broadly based community organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies for Army demonstration teams and static displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Special conditions for Golden Knights, parachute teams, and other demonstration teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Golden Knights considered for public events that connect public with Army and enhance recruitment; appearances on installations only for official open houses. All sponsors (military or civilian) must provide vehicles, hotel rooms, and daily show fee. Aerial demonstrations by other teams depend on Army’s ability to provide resources. Static displays require qualified military personnel available to answer questions and placards with basic specs encouraged. Flight demonstrations with multiple maneuvers should provide narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special conditions for gubernatorial inaugural flyovers
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for ARNG flyovers of gubernatorial inaugural ceremonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governor’s office must request flyover with DD Form 2535. Participating aircraft limited to ARNG resources assigned to the state/territory; states may not request aircraft from other states. Flyover limited to no more than four aircraft and one service component (either ARNG or ANG, not both). Multiple flyovers/aerial reviews prohibited. Flyover must occur during actual inauguration ceremony at a patriotic juncture and be coordinated with federal/state aviation agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and limits on aerial demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational and policy restrictions on aerial demonstrations and related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army aerial assets may not compete for prize money. Charges for admission to Army aircraft/equipment are prohibited; sale of photos of attendees seated in Army aircraft/equipment prohibited. Aerial demonstrations normally limited to 2 days per event (parachute demonstrations up to 3 days), with possible waivers for audience changes, travel considerations, or national/international events. Aircraft performance record demonstrations restricted to aircraft assigned to an operational unit for at least 6 months. Demonstrations implying competition between services not authorized. A nonparticipating Army aviator acts as controller for Army-only demonstrations; a senior military controller designated for multi-service. Controller responsibilities: coordinate sponsor/participants, ensure flight/safety regs observed, and ensure flying time used for readiness/training. Assault aircraft demonstrations/helicopter troop landings under simulated tactical conditions restricted to installations capable of supporting them. Event sponsor required to obtain FAA waiver for public demonstrations; FAA waiver normally required at least 60 days prior. Support depends on availability of resources and should maximize recruiting advantage via coordination with recruiting battalion and PA office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement programs — official examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of official command-initiated programs effective in informing the public and sustaining relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official programs include: active speaker’s bureau, ongoing liaison with external organizations, participatory membership in civic/business/professional organizations, exhibits/bands/color guards/ceremonial units in the public domain, periodic open houses, regular installation tour program, participating in national holiday observances, supporting overseas host nation activities, and supporting local veterans/military service organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial community engagement and off-duty participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on unofficial programs and private participation of military personnel in community activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders should encourage military/civilian personnel and their Families to participate as private persons. Military personnel lending voluntary support during off-duty time may be authorized to participate in uniform if consistent with DoD 5500.07-R; see AR 670–1 for appropriate off-duty uniform wear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison with civilian persons and organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for commanders to maintain community liaison and support local cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must maintain continual liaison to resolve common problems and develop cooperation between installation and local community by: (1) developing effective two-way communication channels; (2) fostering cooperation among civilian and military agencies; (3) providing maximum support of Army activities (AFW and other events); (4) supporting recruiting mission and promoting benefits of Army enlistment; (5) participating in/hosting civic/professional/business club luncheons; (6) promoting USMA and ROTC scholarship opportunities through educators/counselors; (7) promoting use of ARNG armories or USAR centers by civic organizations; (8) ensuring official civilian advisory committees/councils comply with AR 15–1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal community engagement working groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouragement to form informal community engagement groups to coordinate local outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders are encouraged to organize informal working groups comprising key military/civilian staff and subordinate commanders and civilian community counterparts. At minimum, these forums should plan a continuous community engagement program and establish/maintain contact with civilian service, business, economic, professional, minority, veterans, and other organizations.
